newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slips sharply on dlr demand from east.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slips sharply on dlr demand from east.

text.p: The Indian rupee dropped sharply to 35.88/90 per dollar in late trade on Monday on sustained buying from a large state-run bank based in east India, dealers said.
"It (the state-run bank) has been hitting the market for dollars in a big way for the past half hour," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "This has pushed the rupee down."
Earlier, the rupee opened at 35.79/80 per dollar and was largely range-bound between 35.79 and 35.81 for much of Monday, dealers said.
They attributed the late demand to remittances by state-run firms, particularly oil firms.
The dollar was quoted 35.86/88 rupees in latest deals.
